thread:
jen: Quick sync — I sketched a proposal to add a lightweight control-plane shim for tenant routing decisions. The idea: publish a compact, versioned routing hint per-tenant that edge proxies can cache. This would let proxies make region-affinity/residency decisions locally without a remote call for the common case. Questions: API shape, fallback semantics, and how this interacts with active/active failover and legal residency flags.

ravi: What do you mean by 'shim' vs just putting hints in the client header? If proxies lose the cache how do we recover?

jen: Shim = small manifest stored in our control plane (config store) + reconciler that streams diffs to proxies. Proxies keep a TTL'd local copy. If cache miss, proxy either consults fallback heuristics (X-Region-Preferred or nearest region) or does a synchronous lookup to control plane depending on mode.

ian: I like versioned manifests + ETag so proxies can do conditional fetches. Also need an emergency override path (operator-initiated) that bypasses usual cache TTLs.

chris: From an interface standpoint: a single header could be enough for most requests: `X-Rd-Routing: tenant=abc123;ver=3;mode=local;residency=eu:hard;pref=eu-west-1,eu-central-1`. Proxies interpret `residency=eu:hard` as immutable constraint — no cross-region routing even on overload unless explicit operator override.

tess: Legal concern: hard residency means we must also ensure telemetry/trace & logs don't leave region. If proxies enforce routing but traces are forwarded to central collectors in another region, we've violated residency. We need an explicit residency-scope attachment that travels with calls.

ravi: Operational memory/cpu cost: storing full manifests for millions of tenants in every proxy is heavy. Options: (1) compact per-tenant bitset / bloom filter style, (2) store only tenants active in a proxy's shard, (3) pointers to authoritative cluster with remote fallback. Each has tradeoffs for latency and availability.

jen: Agreed. Proposal: support two modes per-tenant: `local` (manifest cached at proxy; low latency, higher memory) and `remote` (proxy performs lightweight control-plane lookup on cache miss; lower memory, slightly higher P99). Default to `remote` for low-volume tenants and `local` for high-volume / enterprise customers.

ian: For failover semantics: when a region is fully degraded, proxies should consult the manifest version: if `residency=soft` allow cross-region failover with audit; if `hard` then fail requests with a clear 409/451-like response and emit an operator alert. We should standardize the status code and an audit event.

chris: Suggest `451-RD-RESIDENCY` with structured JSON body explaining allowed regions and current reason for denial. Also emit a `residency.override` event when ops force-routes for emergency.

tess: Test requirements: simulate full eu-west outage and verify that `soft` tenants failover and `hard` tenants are blocked; ensure traces/logs remain in-region for `hard`. Need a harness and runbook.

ravi: Telemetry: record manifest version used, decision reason (local-cache|remote-lookup|fallback-nearest), and outcome (routed|blocked|failed-over). Sampling at high volume but full logs for enterprise tenants.

jen: API sketch (very rough):
```
GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing-hint
Response 200 {
  "mode": "local|remote",
  "residency": "eu:hard|eu:soft|global",
  "prefer_regions": ["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"],
  "version": "2026-03-21-1"
}
```
Proxies use version to reconcile and to short-circuit fetches.

ian: Need ACLs on who can mutate the manifest and an approvals flow for `hard` residency flags (legal sign-off). Also retention rules for old versions.

ops-bot: deploy: region-routing-shim v1 canary -> eu-west-1 scheduled 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC :rocket:

tess: Follow-up: include test vector for KMS/HSM location enforcement if keys are region-bound. Also add an audit trail for any operator override lasting > 5m.

ravi: Minor optimization idea: publish wildcard rules for multi-tenant orgs so a single rule can cover many tenant IDs instead of per-tenant manifest for some customers. Saves memory and sync bandwidth.

jen: Good note. Also thinking about migration: start with `remote` mode defaults, turn on `local` caching for a small set of high-volume tenants and measure memory. Then consider an auto-promote heuristic based on QPS and SLA.

chris: We should include a short RFC appendix on the expected lifecycle: create -> update (version bump) -> revoke/override -> garbage-collect. Include operator safety gates for `hard`.

jen: Action items: I'll draft RFC with API proto, reconciliation flow, canary plan, and test matrix (including eu outage simulation + trace locality). Can you all review? Please +1 or comment by EOD tomorrow.

ian: +1 for the RFC scope. I'll add the ETag/streaming details.

ravi: +1 on progressive rollout and wildcard rules investigation.

tess: +1 but will add legal checklist for `hard` flags.

chris: +1 and will draft status-code spec and audit event schema.

jen: Thanks — drafting now.
